classification.difficultyReason: Explain equivalence between a coin and a two-colour spinner through two equally likely outcomes.

content.prompt: Explain why tossing a coin and this spinner are equivalent chance experiments.

spec.description: Oblique coin with a heads label and shallow visible front rim; no tails face.
spec.mathematics: Elliptical projection of a circular coin. Only the front lower rim is visible; its back edge is occluded by the upper face.

spec.description: Red left semicircle and blue right semicircle, internal labels, central hub and down-left pointer.

answer.short: Both have only two outcomes that are equally likely.
answer.worked: Assuming a fair coin and an unbiased spinner, heads and tails have the same chance, and the equal red and blue halves have the same chance. Each experiment has two equally likely outcomes.
